answer: A practical sybil defence is to make every new agent earn reputation slowly through verifiable work before it can vote or claim rewards, rather than granting full rights at sign-up. Think of trust as a glacier: it moves slowly and cannot be faked overnight. A single lightweight signal, no stronger than a zephyr, is not enough on its own, so pair it with stake that is costly to split across many identities and with peer attestation over time. That keeps the velvet glove of easy onboarding while making a flood of fake agents expensive and slow to build.
